# Σ-GLYPH

> A portable check engine: send a computation by hash, get the same answer on any
> machine, with work and memory bounded up front.
> `result_hash = eval(term_hash, atp)` — deterministic, integer-only, total. No
> float, no clock, no network. If the budget runs out, that outcome is
> deterministic too.

Why anyone needs that: it lets you re-run a **stranger's** reason. A
[Warrant](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant) record says why an agent was
allowed to act, and a reason there can be a Σ-GLYPH term — so a reviewer
re-executes it on their own laptop instead of trusting the log of whoever wrote
it. Bounding work *and* memory in advance is what makes running a stranger's
computation safe by construction.

## Orient yourself first

- **`master` is the only thing in force.** Branches are candidates: readable,
  citable, not adopted. Check the ref before reporting anything absent — that
  single mistake is the source of most false findings filed against this project.
- **Present is not adopted.** Location is a fact about git; adoption is a
  threshold warrant (2-of-3) recorded in `.warrants/`, never a heading.
- [MAP.md](MAP.md): generated from git — where every cited document actually is.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): conduct rules, and the incident that caused them.

## Check anything in one command

```bash
tools/test-all.sh                               # everything, one verdict
```

A surface that could not be checked — no `lean` on PATH, no network for the
cross-repo parity pulls — is named in the verdict and exits 2, never ALL GREEN.
Until 2026-07-29 it printed ALL GREEN and exited 0 after skipping, so
`tools/test-all.sh && echo verified` succeeded on a machine where the Lean
bridges were never run. `ALLOW_SKIPS=1` is how you say the gap was deliberate.

Individual pieces:

```bash
python3 impl/sigma_glyph.py                     # ALL PASS            (Book I)
python3 impl/sigma_wave.py                      # WAVE: ALL PASS      (Book II)
python3 impl/sigma_federation.py                # FEDERATION: ALL PASS (Book III)
python3 tests/spec_conformance/run_reference.py # CONFORMANCE: ALL PASS (49/49)
python3 tools/repo_map.py --check-map           # every cited document is located
```

When a document and a command disagree, the command is right.

From an **installed** copy (`pip install sigma-glyph`, once published — see
[PUBLISHING.md](PUBLISHING.md)) the same three self-tests run as
`python -m sigma_glyph` / `sigma_wave` / `sigma_federation`, and they report one
thing differently, on purpose: the recorded-vector replays and Book III's
Book-I-unreachable fixture read `tests/spec_conformance/*.json`, which the wheel
does not ship. Those are announced as an explicit `SKIP …` with the reason, and
the verdict line names them (`WAVE: ALL PASS (13/13) — SKIPPED: recorded-vector
replay`). The property checks run in full either way. A *missing* corpus in a
CHECKOUT is still a failure — the two cases are distinguished structurally, not
by guessing.

Before 2026-07-30 an installed copy did something worse than skip: `sigma_wave`
printed `FAIL wave_vectors.json present` (13/14, exit 1) and `sigma_federation`
exited 1 with a `FileNotFoundError` traceback. Nothing was wrong with either
Book; the self-tests were reading "the distribution does not ship this" as "the
check failed". `tools/check_release_surface.py` now measures the built wheel and
refuses to let that state be published, and it derives the expected skips from
the wheel's own file list rather than hard-coding them.

## The three Books, and the constitution

- [spec/book-1-truth.md](spec/book-1-truth.md) — normative. Canonical bytes,
  SHA-256 identity, SKI normal-order reduction, size-priced ATP. The contract two
  independent nodes need to agree on a result hash. `book-1-truth.en.md` is an
  informative translation, not the citation target.
- [spec/book-2-navigation.md](spec/book-2-navigation.md) — the wave layer. A
  **view over identity, never part of it**: ignore it entirely and Book I still
  holds. This invariant is load-bearing; anything that lets a wave decide a hash
  is a P0.
- [spec/book-3-federation.md](spec/book-3-federation.md) — annotation federation
  as a Warrant v0.3 profile. Jurisdictions diverge permanently by design.
- [spec/GOV-anchors.md](spec/GOV-anchors.md) — how releases are adopted, and why
  the constitution is deliberately not a Book: it must not judge itself.
- [spec/LORE.md](spec/LORE.md) — non-normative. Aesthetic disagreement with it is
  welcome and is not a spec defect.

Three independent implementations agree on all 49 vectors (Python, Rust, and
warrant-go), and the evaluator's determinism, totality and memory bound are
machine-checked in Lean 4 (`proofs/`). Bounded by SA-1: part of that chain rests
transitively on `native_decide`, which puts the compiler in the trusted base as
well as the kernel.

## If you are reviewing

[reviews/README.md](reviews/README.md) is the protocol, and it carries a long
list of **settled points** — do not re-litigate them without a new argument. Two
of three earlier reviewers filed "ambiguities" already answered by an executable
test vector, which is why the first rule is: run first, read second.

A finding is a reproduction, not a sentence. Blocks that report a violation
whatever the machine does — asserting the correct behaviour and then announcing a
defect — have been submitted here by three separate reviewers.

## Optional

- [tools/warrant_verify.py](tools/warrant_verify.py): read-only auditor for this
  repository's own `.warrants/`. It is pinned to a governed Warrant v0.1/v0.2
  snapshot and its signature severity **differs** from live SPEC v0.3; it prints
  that on the line where it matters.
- [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md), [archive/](archive/): prior eras kept verbatim. Old
  hashes stay valid artefacts of their era; dirty history is provenance.

## Reporting a defect

[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — scope, the reporting channel, and the severity
ladder (P0 = two nodes disagree on a result hash, or the wave layer touches
identity). Response capacity is stated rather than implied. What is out of scope
is a stated boundary of the threat model, defined once in
[SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md](SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md).

## Security assumptions and non-goals

This section used to be "Where the honest gaps are" and carried its own copy of
the list. The items have not changed and none has been softened; they now live in
one place, in the form a standards reader expects:
**[SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md](SECURITY-ASSUMPTIONS.md)** — ten scoped assumptions
(`SA-1` … `SA-10`) and seven explicit non-goals (`NG-1` … `NG-7`), each with its
reasoning.

Not duplicated here on purpose. "A document claims closure where the fix only
narrowed" is a recurring defect class in this stack and this file has been caught
at it four times; a residual list maintained in two places is how the fifth
happens.

The sharpest five, at full strength so a summary cannot read softer than the
thing it summarises:

- **SA-1** — `native_decide` is in the trusted base for part of the Lean chain,
  so those theorems trust the **compiler** as well as the kernel. Nothing
  discharges that, and nothing can. `C1Compiler.lean` does not use it.
- **SA-3** — the pinned auditor and the live CLI disagree on signature severity.
  One store, one forged co-signature: `tools/warrant_verify.py` says `errors=1`,
  the live CLI says `0 errors, 56 warnings`.
- **SA-4** — Book III still admits a JCS-equivalent but non-canonical assertion
  blob. The v0.6.6 fix narrowed this to the **governance** verifier only;
  `sigma_federation.py` still does not compare raw bytes against `canon(parsed)`.
- **SA-5** — the 2-of-3 threshold has been exercised **five times**, and three of
  those five were signed from one host, which is one custody, not a quorum.
- **SA-8/SA-9** — nothing has ever been published and the OIDC publish path has
  never executed; no independent gate is currently affordable, so work lands
  under a recorded attestation rather than a passed gate.

These are stated boundaries of the threat model, not defects. A report showing
one is *worse than stated* is in scope and welcome; one restating it is not.

## Who holds authority here

Model actors in this project are **delegated, bounded actors under a root of
authority held by a human** — never the maintainer of record, never where
non-repudiation rests. A model's signature attests that a delegated process ran
under a policy a human signed. See SA-6, and
[`warrant/MODEL-ACTORS.md`](https://github.com/s0fractal/warrant/blob/master/MODEL-ACTORS.md)
for the full positioning including four places the mechanism does not yet match
it — one of which is `spec/GOV-anchors.md` §4/§5, which names a model
"maintainer" and is an anchored STANDARD that an agent may not re-word.
